If the number of people who could do at least two of these things, was found to be 37 and the number of people who could do all these things was found to be 6, how many people could not do any of these things?
example.rationale:
T=n(A)+n(B)+n(C)-n(Exactly two of the events)-2*n(All 3 Events)+n(None of the events)
T=144
n(A)=T-n(A')=144-85=59
n(B)=T-n(B')=144-100=44
n(C)=T-n(C')=144-91=53
n(Exactly two of the events)=n(At least 2 Events)-n(All 3 Events)=37-6=31
n(All 3 Events)=6
144=59+44+53-31-2*6+n(None of the events)
n(None of the events)=144-55-44-53+31+12=31
Ans:B

example.question: A and B start a business, with A investing the total capital of Rs.100000, on the condition that B pays A interest @ 10% per annum on his half of the capital. A is a working partner and receives Rs.10000 per month from the total profit and any profit remaining is equally shared by both of them. At the end of the year, it was found that the income of A is twice that of B. Find the total profit for the year?
example.rationale:
Interest received by A from B = 10% of half of Rs.100000 = 10% * 50000 = 5000.
Amount received by A per annum for being a working partner = 10000 * 12 = Rs.120000.
Let 'P' be the part of the remaining profit that A receives as his share. Total income of A = (5000+ 120000 + P)
Total income of B = only his share from the remaining profit = 'P', as A and B share the remaining profit equally.
Income of A = Twice the income of B
(5000 + 120000 + P) = 2(P)
P = 125000
Total profit = 2P + 120000
= 2*125000 + 120000 = 2620000
Answer:B
